## introduction
As one of the most popular drinks in the world, coffee has a rich and profound knowledge system. From the cultivation and processing of coffee beans, to roasting, brewing, and tasting, every step contains countless knowledge and skills. This report will comprehensively explore all aspects of the coffee world and help readers gain a deeper understanding of this fascinating beverage culture.
## Chapter 1: Types and Characteristics of Coffee Beans
### 1.1 Main coffee bean varieties
Coffee beans are mainly divided into two categories: Arabica and Robusta.
### Arabica coffee beans
- Proportion: Accounts for more than 70% of global coffee production
- Growth environment: high altitude areas (above 800 meters), requiring mild climate conditions
- Flavor characteristics: soft taste, high acidity, rich aroma, floral and fruity aroma
- Price: Relatively high, good quality
- Representative production areas: Ethiopia, Colombia, Kenya, Jamaica Blue Mountain, etc.
### robusta coffee beans
- Proportion: accounts for about 30% of global coffee production
- Growth environment: low altitude areas (200-800 meters), strong adaptability, strong resistance to diseases and pests
- Flavor characteristics: strong taste, heavy bitterness, high caffeine content (about twice that of Arabica)
- Price: relatively low
- Usage: Commonly used in blending instant coffee and espresso
### 1.2 Famous coffee producing areas
Coffee beans from different producing areas have unique terroir characteristics:
- Ethiopia: Hara, Yirgacheffe, with bright acidity and floral aromas
- Kenya: Kenya AA, with prominent acidity and blackcurrant flavor
- Jamaica: Blue Mountain Coffee, with excellent balance, is known as the King of Coffee
- Colombia: mellow taste, balance of sour and sweet
- Brazil: Santos, suitable as a base for blended beans
## Chapter 2: Coffee making process
### 2.1 Main brewing methods
### Pour Over
- Features: Can highlight the flavor characteristics of coffee and have a clear taste
- Applicable beans: single-origin beans, especially coffee with bright flavors
- Appliances: V60, Chemex, Kalita Wave, etc.
- Tips: control water temperature (90-96°C), grinding degree (medium-fine), water injection speed and time
### French Press
- Features: High mellowness, retaining coffee oil, and full taste
- Applicable beans: dark roasted beans
- Grinding degree: Coarse grinding
- Soaking time: 4 minutes
### Espresso
- Features: high concentration and concentrated flavor, which is the basis for making various fancy coffees
- Pressure: 9 atmospheres
- Extraction time: 20-30 seconds
- Grinding degree: very fine grinding
### AeroPress
- Features: Strong portability, short extraction time, clean taste
- Applicable scenarios: travel, office
- Extraction time: 1-2 minutes
### 2.2 Factors affecting brewing quality
1. Grinding: Different brewing methods require different grinding thicknesses
1. Water temperature: generally controlled between 90-96°C
1. Pink to water ratio: usually 1:15 to 1:17
1. Extraction time: Depends on brewing method
1. Water quality: water with moderate softness and hardness is the best
## Chapter 3: Coffee Roasting and Tasting
### 3.1 Coffee roasting
Roasting is the key process that transforms green coffee beans into brewable coffee beans:
### Roasting degree classification
- Light roasting: retains more original bean flavor and bright acidity
- Medium roast: balances acidity and bitterness, suitable for most tastes
- Dark roast: prominent bitterness and high degree of caramelization
### Effect of roasting on flavor
- Time control: standard baking time is 8-16 minutes
- Temperature curve: precise control of heating rate is required
- First burst and second burst: important baking node indicators
### 3.2 Coffee cupping (Cupping)
Cupping is a standardized method of assessing coffee quality:
### Cupping steps
1. Dry Aroma Assessment: Smell the aroma of ground coffee
1. Wet aroma evaluation: smell the aroma of rising steam after filling with water
1. Breaking the grounds: Use a spoon to stir and remove surface coffee grounds
1. Tasting: Sip the coffee liquid with a special spoon
### Assessment Dimensions
- Aroma: the intensity and quality of dry and wet aromas
- Flavor: the taste characteristics felt in the mouth
- Acidity: brightness and liveliness
- Body: The thickness of the mouthfeel
- Aftertaste: the lingering taste after swallowing
- Balance: the coordination of various flavor elements
- Cleanliness (Clean Cup): Is there any defective taste?
- Sweetness: the degree of natural sweetness
### 3.3 Flavor description
The coffee flavor wheel helps us describe the taste of coffee more accurately:
### Main flavor categories
- Fruity aroma: citrus, berries, tropical fruits
- Floral fragrance: jasmine, rose, lavender
- Nuts: almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts
- Chocolate: cocoa, dark chocolate, milk chocolate
- Spices: cinnamon, cloves, pepper
## Chapter 4: Modern Coffee Culture
### 4.1 Specialty coffee movement
The third wave of coffee emphasizes:
- Single-origin coffee: highlighting the characteristics of the origin
- Traceability: complete information from farm to cup
- Handcrafted: focus on brewing skills and personalization
- Sustainable development: focus on environmental protection and fair trade
### 4.2 Coffee and health
Health benefits of drinking coffee in moderation:
- Antioxidant: rich in polyphenols
- Increased alertness: the positive effects of caffeine
- Reduce disease risk: May reduce the risk of certain diseases
## in conclusion
Coffee knowledge is a broad and profound field. From the selection of coffee beans to the final tasting, every link is worthy of in-depth study and exploration. Whether we are professional practitioners or coffee enthusiasts, mastering these basics can help us better appreciate and enjoy the wonderful world of coffee.
By systematically learning coffee bean types, production techniques, roasting techniques and tasting methods, we can:
- Choose coffee beans that suit your taste preferences
- Master the tips and tricks of different brewing methods
- Develop a keen sense of taste
- Deeply understand the connotation of coffee culture
Coffee is not just a drink, but a lifestyle and cultural experience. In this world full of aroma and flavor, every cup of coffee tells a unique story, waiting for us to discover and taste it.
